newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks wobble on Kohl rumours, close higher.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks wobble on Kohl rumours, close higher.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed with slight gains on Thursday after volatile late trade unsettled by rumours, immediately denied by Germany, that Chancellor Helmut Kohl had died or was seriously sick.
Dealers said seasonal slowness made the market vulnerable to such rumours.
The general index was up 2.54 points, 0.42 percent, at 602.40 and the Ibex-35 gained 29.01 points, 0.42 percent, to 6,864.11.
"Despite the scarce foundation of these rumours, unique to months like August, they have affected derivatives and triggered arbitrage operations with futures buying and cash sales," one dealer said.
The banking sector was a big draw and trading was heavy.

"Buying banks is the best way for end investors to enter the growing economy. In addition, the sector is not expensive compared to other foreign banks and the last half results have been better than expected," another dealer said.
BBV, with a gain of 2.63 percent, had the biggest jump among Ibex shares and was the third most traded.
Repsol fell 70 pesetas to 6,350, retracing part of a big rise on Wednesday after first half results.
